Explainer storyboard

Ask CrowdPulse: answers you can watch

A 3:28 film about the question-answering tool in ask/. The pages on screen are the real tool. The answers are real too: recorded runs of Claude Code, replayed at the speed they happened, and passed through the tool's checks again on every render. Every image is a real frame of the render (from the 1440p master, shown at 1280×720), and the narration is the script the Kokoro af_heart voice reads. Scenes come from film/ask/ask-film.js; re-render with film/render_ask.py.

0:00Cold open

Shows
A question about the code, and the idea: ask it, and watch the answer
Camera
The map lies tilted in the dark with an answer running across it, then swings up to face the viewer
Sound
Music swells in; key taps as the question types; whoosh on the title

0:00Some questions about a codebase take an afternoon to answer. How does a rating get from a phone, to the big screen?

0:08What if you could just ask? And then watch the answer happen.

0:16Asking a question

Shows
Typing a question, choosing who is asking, and the answer streaming in while the animation already plays
Camera
Full window for the typing; pushes in on the answer; then rides along with the packet across the map
Sound
Key taps, a click on Ask, soft pops as steps land

0:17This is Ask CrowdPulse. It runs on your own machine, right next to the code. Type a question, say who’s asking, and press Ask.

0:28Claude Code reads the repository. A few seconds later, a short answer appears, and then the steps start to arrive. The animation begins before the answer has finished.

0:42Each step is one claim. Something travels between two parts of the app, and the caption says what it is.

0:52Phone, to connection, to database. Then back out, on a broadcast, to every screen.

1:01Why you can trust it

Shows
Every step quotes a real line that is looked up first; a step between unconnected parts is dropped; an invented quote is flagged
Camera
Pushes in on a step’s citation while the real file scrolls to the quoted line; pulls back for the two planted mistakes
Sound
Chime when a quote is found; a dull pop when it is not

1:01Here’s why you can trust it. Every step quotes a line of the real code, and that quote is looked up in the file before the step is shown.

1:13To show what happens when the model gets it wrong, we planted two mistakes in this answer.

1:21This step jumps between two parts that aren’t connected on the map. It never reaches the screen.

1:30And this one quotes a line that isn’t in the file. It’s shown, but flagged as unverified.

1:39A verified step proves the line exists. Whether the caption reads it correctly is still your call, so the line is always one click away.

1:50How it works

Shows
The fixed map and its anchors; what Claude is given and what it sends back; how quickly the first step arrived
Camera
The map alone, tilted, as its anchors appear; then the map beside what goes in and what comes out
Sound
Soft pops as anchors and lines appear

1:50Under the hood, the map is fixed. Eighteen parts of the app and the connections between them, each one anchored to a line of code.

2:01Claude doesn’t draw anything. It gets the map and an outline of the code, and replies with a list of steps, one per line.

2:13Because the map is already on screen, the answer can start playing as soon as the first line lands. Here, that took about four seconds.

2:23One question, three audiences

Shows
The same question answered for a developer, an architect and a product owner, playing side by side
Camera
Three windows in a row, each with its current caption underneath
Sound
Whoosh as the three windows arrive

2:24The same question can be asked three ways. A developer gets function names.

2:32An architect gets boundaries and trade-offs. A product owner gets plain language.

2:41Same map, same code, three different stories.

2:46Answers that can’t go stale

Shows
The six prepared examples playing at once, and the real test run that checks every quoted line
Camera
A wall of six maps; a terminal runs the tests over it
Sound
Soft ticks as tests pass; chime on the summary

2:47The prepared examples double as tests. Every one has to play on the map, and every quoted line has to exist in the code today.

2:57Change a line that an answer depends on, and the test run fails and names the quote. The explanations can’t quietly go stale.

Shows
The three things the tool does, then how to start it
Camera
The wall of maps tips back into the distance behind three lines of text; end card
Sound
Music resolves; whoosh on the end card

3:08Ask CrowdPulse. Ask a question. Watch the answer. Check the line.

3:17To try it, run npm run ask, and open localhost, port thirty-one hundred.
